sentences.text: Lava Heights Academy is a residential treatment center in Toquerville, Utah, run since October 2021 by Rite of Passage.
It opened in 2012, took both boys and girls for most of its history, and now serves girls.
It has passed through three owners, including Sequel Youth and Family Services, which closed two of its other Utah programs amid abuse investigations in 2019.
In 2023 Paul Anthony Nichols, a staff member there, was sent to prison for sexually abusing two girls he supervised.
Former employees have published accounts of the program since 2018 (see Survivor testimony below).

sentences.text: The Centers for Adolescent Recovery and Education (CARE) built Lava Heights and opened it in 2012 as a treatment program centered on the performing arts.
It sits at 730 Spring Drive in Toquerville.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing, facility record and inspection findings for license 94202 (Care Youth Corporation dba Rite of Passage / Lava Heights Academy)

sentences.text: In 2016 Sequel Youth and Family Services acquired it along with three other Utah programs, Falcon Ridge Ranch, Red Rock Canyon School and Mount Pleasant Academy.
In July 2019 Sequel closed Red Rock Canyon School and Mount Pleasant Academy amid investigations into abuse.
Sequel ran Lava Heights until the fall of 2021: its website still named Sequel on September 28, 2021, and by October 20 it named Rite of Passage as the operator.
Utah has licensed it to Care Youth Corporation, doing business as Rite of Passage, since January 31, 2022.

sources.cite: Utah Office of Licensing, facility record and inspection findings for license 94202 (Care Youth Corporation dba Rite of Passage / Lava Heights Academy)

sentences.text: In February 2018 The Spectrum reported that two boys had run away from Lava Heights and were missing for nearly four days.
One of their mothers said staff did not file a missing-person report or ask police to publicize the disappearance.
In September 2022 Lava Heights hired Paul Anthony Nichols, 22, of St. George, to supervise girls in the program.
Three days later he started a game of "truth or dare" with students he supervised.

Two girls under 16 told detectives he touched them inappropriately on at least eight occasions, including sexual abuse in the facility's restrooms, and that he photographed one of them partly undressed.
Officials received the first report on October 20, 2022, and Nichols was arrested in December and charged with rape, forcible sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of a minor.
He admitted to investigators that he had touched the girls on multiple occasions and photographed one.
On March 28, 2023, he pleaded guilty to five counts of forcible sexual abuse and two of sexual exploitation of a minor, and the rape charge was dismissed.
On May 16, 2023, Judge Jay Winward sentenced him to 1 to 15 years in prison on each count, to run concurrently, and ordered him to register as a sex offender.
State inspectors have kept finding violations since Rite of Passage took over.

testimony.text: I was an employee at Lava Heights Academy. … The choices that are made for by upper management are based strictly off of what will bring in the most money and NOT what will help these kids. … There were a handful of staff that actually cared about the students' growth and expressed their concerns to upper management, and the next thing you know those individuals were let go. Lava Heights should be shut down for the things that have taken place here. I have reported several incidents to the Sequel's compliance Manager and still nothing was done. … Some incidents included: … MANY med errors where incident reports "magically" disappeared … Inappropriate restraints and Management would tell staff a specific way to word the incident report …
They abuse the residents and try to blame the staff. … They hurt kids and blame staff. This is not a safe environment for anyone, staff or resident.
